aiDataConsent.title: Your messages go to the AI you choose
aiDataConsent.intro: Unbiase AI does not run its own models. Before your first message, here is where your data goes.
aiDataConsent.modelsBody: Messages, photos and files you send go to the provider of the model you pick. Chat titles and memory use your primary provider. Always on your own API keys.
aiDataConsent.memoryBody: When memory or chat indexing is on, conversation text goes to the embedding service and vector database you connected, on your own accounts. So do your search words. You can switch memory and indexing off in Settings.
aiDataConsent.webBody: When the model searches the web or uses a tool you connected, its search terms or tool inputs go to that service, on your own account.
aiDataConsent.note: Each service handles your data under its own terms. See your connected services and review this any time in Settings.

toolsSettings.activateHelp: A tool can be turned on once a dry run has succeeded.
toolsSettings.argumentsHelp: The values the assistant fills in when it calls the tool. Use one in the call below by writing {{args.name}} wherever it belongs.

toolsSettings.deleteConfirm: Delete the tool "{{name}}"? Assistants using it will stop being able to call it.

toolsSettings.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. Create an issue in our tracker and return its identifier.
toolsSettings.dryRunErrorTitle: The dry run could not be made
toolsSettings.dryRunHelp: Makes one real call with the test values. A tool stays a draft until a dry run succeeds.
toolsSettings.errorArgumentDuplicate: Two arguments share a name. Each one needs its own.
toolsSettings.errorArgumentName: Argument names use letters, numbers and underscores, and start with a letter.
toolsSettings.errorArgumentUnknown: The call uses {{name}}, which is not one of the arguments above.
toolsSettings.errorDescriptionLength: The description needs to be between {{min}} and {{max}} characters.
toolsSettings.errorMaxChars: Choose a limit between 1 and {{max}} characters.
toolsSettings.errorNameFormat: Use 3 to 64 characters: lowercase letters, numbers and underscores, starting with a letter.
toolsSettings.errorNameReserved: “{{name}}” is already the name of a built-in tool. Pick another.
toolsSettings.errorPathRequired: Enter the path to the value you want.
toolsSettings.errorTooManyArguments: A tool can take at most {{max}} arguments.
toolsSettings.errorUrlHttps: The address has to start with https://.
toolsSettings.errorUrlOrigin: The address up to the first / is fixed — arguments can only be used from the path onwards.
toolsSettings.maxCharsHelp: Longer responses are cut off at this length before the assistant sees them.
toolsSettings.nameHelp: This is the name the assistant calls. Lowercase letters, numbers and underscores.
toolsSettings.outboundMissing: The server did not report the request it sent.
toolsSettings.rawResponseTitle: 2. The response, as it came back
toolsSettings.rawTruncated: Cut off at the character limit above.
toolsSettings.testValuesHelp: The values a dry run calls with. They are only used for the test.
toolsSettings.testValuesNone: This tool takes no arguments, so a dry run needs no test values.
toolsSettings.transformMode_json: The whole response, as formatted JSON
toolsSettings.transformPathHelp: A dotted path, such as data.issue.identifier. Use a number to pick an item from a list, such as items.0.title.
toolsSettings.urlHelp: Has to start with https://. The address up to the first / is fixed; from the path onwards you can use {{args.name}}.

connectorsSettings.approvalTitle: Approve what your assistants will be told about

connectorsSettings.chooseSpec: An API you have the description for

connectorsSettings.credentialNameHelp: The name the key is stored under. Anything else that uses the same key can share it.
connectorsSettings.disconnectConfirm_one: Disconnect "{{label}}"? This deletes the one tool it added, and assistants using it will stop being able to call it.
connectorsSettings.disconnectConfirm_other: Disconnect "{{label}}"? This deletes all {{count}} tools it added, and assistants using them will stop being able to call them.

block.message: They can't find you by username, share with you or see your shared items, and you can't do those things with them. Shares between you are removed.

blockedUsers.intro: Blocked users can't find you by username, share with you or see your shared items. Blocking works both ways.
blockedUsers.note: Unblocking doesn't bring back shares that were removed. Either of you can share again.

contentRules.title: Content rules
contentRules.scope: Applies to anything you share with other users or make public.
contentRules.intro: Your conversations and instructions are private until you share them. Once another person can see them, they have to follow these rules. We don't read private content to enforce them.
contentRules.reportsBody: Anyone who can see a shared item can report it from its menu. Our team reviews every report promptly. The owner is not told who reported. If the item breaks these rules we make it private, and repeat offenders can lose the ability to share.
contentRules.blockingBody: You can block any user from an item they shared with you, from the share dialog or from Settings › Profile. Blocking works both ways: neither of you can find the other by username, share with the other or see the other's shared items while signed in. Shares between you are removed.
contentRules.contactBody: Questions, appeals or something urgent: <support>genflowly.com/support</support>. The <policy>privacy policy</policy> explains what we store.
list: Harassment, bullying or threats against a person
Hate or discrimination based on who someone is
Sexual content involving minors, or sexual content shared with people who didn't ask for it
Instructions for violence or other serious harm
Illegal activity, or content that belongs to someone else
contentRules.filterNote: An automatic check refuses to share text with slurs or explicit language. It is a first line, not the whole rule.
